newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition threatens to oust government.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition threatens to oust government.

text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition threatened on Thursday to oust the country's newly-elected government, accusing it of human rights violations and political persecution.
"The government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has already proved its failure to run the country," Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) chief Begum Khaleda Zia told a huge rally in Dhaka.

"We have given enough time to this government...but it kept on promoting terrorism, persecuting opponents and violating human rights. Everything is being done from a partisan outlook and we have almost run out of patience," said the former prime minister.
"The people of Bangladesh must now be ready for a campaign to drive the anti-people government from power."
Amid applause and cheers, Khaleda criticised the new government's closer ties to India and warned that Bangladeshis would never tolerate a "subservient" relationship with their giant neighbour.
Hasina's Awami League defeated the BNP in a general election in June, held under a neutral caretaker government and billed as free and peaceful by international monitors.
Khaleda refuses to accept the poll results.
"The election was tampered with and never reflected a popular vote," Khaleda said on Thursday.

Hasina told parliament on Wednesday that the BNP had been trying to oust her government since its first day in office. "They are inciting the armed forces to revolt...and even threatening to kill me."
Khaleda and other BNP leaders at Thursday's rally did not specify their next move, but political analysts say they might resort to a campaign of strikes and transport shutdowns.
"The government is behaving in a way that shuts all doors for our cooperation," Khaleda said in her first public speech in in the capital since June.
